key_insight: Structurally distinct Y6 aggregates enable ultrafast directional energy transfer that supports efficient charge generation in organic homojunction solar cells.
engineering_relevance: Engineering complementary aggregate packing and charge-transfer character could improve organic solar cells without conventional donor–acceptor bulk heterojunctions.
method: Probe inter-aggregate energy transfer using ultrafast spectroscopy.
Relate aggregate structure and charge-transfer character to excited-state dynamics.
Develop a multi-component Förster resonance energy transfer (FRET) framework.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 65% ensemble-averaged FRET efficiency on a sub-picosecond timescale (<1 ps) in Y6 thin films.
watch_item: Generality beyond Y6 and reproducible control of aggregate populations require validation; the abstract describes no AI method.
paper_title: Ultrafast Inter-Aggregate Energy Transfer Drives Efficient Charge Generation in Organic Homojunctions
